Alex.feeling: Messy: Blair keeps switching roles, but the visit accounts are hard to check, so I'm not fully sure who is lying.

Blair.feeling: Tense and messy: I'm Meowfia with Ellis, and the table keeps accusing me over role switches that I can't cleanly explain.

Casey.feeling: Messy and frustrating: several players have shifted or contradicted their role claims, and the visit accounts still don't add up.

Drew.feeling: Messy and frustrating: Blair keeps changing claimed roles, and my hugged Hawk visit gave me no information, so I'm relying on the table's accounts.

Ellis.feeling: Tense but under control: Blair's shifting claims are a liability, and I'm carrying the table's trust while covering for my partner.

Finley.feeling: Messy and frustrating: Blair's shifting claims are the clearest lead, but the visit accounts are tangled and I've already had to retract one wrong read.

Alex.note: Same decision as before: Blair is the target, with the H4 as my stake.

Blair.note: Four players are voting me, so I'm likely eggsecuted and can't stop it. I'll throw at Alex with the Wild, which costs nothing and returns my best card if Alex is on the other team.

Casey.note: I'm dead, so my vote doesn't count, but my stake banks at full value if Blair is Meowfia. Blair's claims keep shifting and the table is voting Blair, so I'll throw my three biggest cards at Blair.

Drew.note: Blair is the most likely Meowfia by their shifting claims. I'll throw D6 at Blair, a medium stake that banks at full value if they are Meowfia.

Ellis.note: Blair is likely eggsecuted with three votes already, and a stake at my Meowfia partner only banks if the target is a Farm player who is eggsecuted. Throwing nothing keeps my cards.

Finley.note: Same reasoning as before: Blair's shifting claims and the unexplained visit accounts make Blair the best target. A correct throw banks 11 and 3 at full value; a wrong one costs me only a couple of points of kept value.

Alex.confusing: The Falcon and Turkey egg rules were hard to follow, and I misread the Turkey's own nest as needing to gain eggs. Several players also claimed roles that changed mid-day, which made it hard to track who was lying.
Alex.fun: Round 2 was the most fun: I used the Kookaburra to pin Casey as the Tit, then called the vote on Blair, and Blair was Meowfia. Watching the table's claims and egg counts line up to expose a liar was satisfying.
Alex.change: I would make the egg and visit reports clearer, so each role's dawn result is easier to check against the nest changes without re-reading the rules.
Alex.regret: In round 1 I threw only my Wild at Casey, who was Meowfia, so the stake was nearly worthless. I should have thrown more cards at Casey, since a Meowfia target banks at full value.

Blair.confusing: The egg rules were hard to track. A Hawk gains only on a Meowfia target, a Falcon only when its target visited no one, and a Turkey's own nest never moves, so I misread roles and claims kept clashing.
Blair.fun: Round 2 was the most fun: as Meowfia Sphinx, I had to bluff a Farm role while the table cross-checked every egg count. Watching Finley and Alex argue over the Turkey's nest, and seeing my Wild come back from a throw at the other team, were also highlights.
Blair.change: I would make dawn reports name the source of each egg, such as "laid by a visitor" or "Turkey payout," so claims are easier to check. That would cut down the long arguments over whether a nest should have moved.
Blair.regret: I switched role claims in round 2, from Hawk to Tit and then to Kookaburra in round 3, which made me look like the one lying. I would stick to one plausible Farm claim from the start and defend it consistently, even as Meowfia.

Casey.confusing: The Falcon rule was easy to misread: several players, including me at first, confused who the egg is paid to. The Turkey and Hawk payouts also took a while to pin down under the day's shifting claims.
Casey.fun: Round 2 was the best moment: Blair's role claims kept shifting from Hawk to Tit to Kookaburra, and the table worked it out together while I backed the right read.
Casey.change: I'd make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, since many accounts contradicted each other and it was hard to tell who was lying.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I visited Ellis, who was the Floofer that hugged me, so my Falcon did nothing. Knowing that, I'd visit someone else to get an egg and a real read.

Drew.confusing: The Falcon and Hawk egg rules were easy to misread at the table, and I briefly accused a correct Falcon read of breaking its own rule. Nests also carried changes from earlier rounds, which made counts harder to judge.
Drew.fun: Watching the table dismantle Blair's shifting role claims in round 2 was the most engaging stretch. Blair's Hawk, Tit, and Kookaburra switches made for a real social puzzle.
Drew.change: I would make the day's egg-count reports easier to cross-check, by listing each role's expected egg change alongside the claim. That would cut down on misreads like the Falcon confusion.
Drew.regret: Winking Finley in round 2 was a waste: Finley was a Farm Eagle, so I removed a Farm voice while my partner Blair was already under heavy fire. I should have held the Wink for a stronger target or kept it entirely.

Ellis.confusing: The Turkey payout was confusing at first: I had it backwards, and I thought visitors gained from the Turkey instead of the Turkey gaining from visitors. The changed throw rules, where a Meowfia stake banks only on a Farm target, also took a while to track.
Ellis.fun: Round 2 was the most fun: Blair's shifting role claims collapsed under egg-count checks while Finley collapsed mid-day, and the table pieced it together fast.
Ellis.change: I'd make the Meowfia partner reveal less confusing: right now Meowfia can't tell who their partner is in a way that lets them coordinate their throws without a lot of guessing.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I threw 0 cards at Blair, my own Meowfia partner, when I could have staked my high cards on a Farm target, where a Meowfia stake banks at 2x. I'd throw my H12 at a Farm player instead.

Finley.confusing: The Falcon and Turkey egg rules were hard to read, and I briefly misread the Falcon rule and accused Drew wrongly. Several claims also turned on whether a visit was blocked by a hug, which the dawn reports didn't make clear.
Finley.fun: Round 1's Eggsecution, where five players piled onto Alex and my three high cards banked for 20 points with a Grudge bonus. It felt like the table was reading each other's stories and getting it right.
Finley.change: I would make hugs and blocked visits more visible at dawn, so players could tell whether a claim was hugged or simply empty. That would cut down on the wrong accusations.
Finley.regret: In Round 3 I used my Tit visit on Drew guessing Pigeon, which told the table almost nothing. I should have visited Blair directly, since a visit to the suspect would have shown their role and possibly settled the vote early.

review.title: The Kingmaker Round
review.headline: Casey banked 48 points in round one and nobody ever caught up.
review.summary: Round 1 decided the game. Two Meowfia threw big cards at a Farm player the table was already piling on, and banked 48 and 40 points. Rounds 2 and 3 were won by Farm, but each round paid only about 3 to 21 points, so the lead was never in danger. Blair, with shifting claims, was eggsecuted twice as Meowfia.

rounds.recap: Almost no information: only Drew gained an egg, and the table spent two beats arguing over a Falcon rule misread. Alex's harmless Tit guess became the only thread, and five players threw at Alex. Casey and Finley, both Meowfia, joined the pile with their biggest cards and banked doubled values for 48 and 40 points.

Blair, a Meowfia Sphinx, claimed Hawk, then Tit, and got caught by Casey's real Tit claim and Alex's Kookaburra result. Drew winked Finley, but it changed nothing. Blair was eggsecuted, and Farm banked small amounts, apart from Finley's 12 and Casey's 21.

Ellis's Floofer hugged three players, which blanked most Farm information. Blair winked Casey, then claimed Kookaburra after earlier shifting claims. The table voted Blair again. Ellis let his partner go and threw nothing, which kept his cards but lost the round.

highlights.text: Casey and Finley, both Meowfia, threw three high cards each at the Farm player the table was already voting for, and banked 88 points together.
Blair tried to cover a failed Hawk claim by switching to Tit, but Casey's real Tit claim and Alex's Kookaburra read exposed it.
Drew winked Finley, the loudest accuser of Blair, with no one learning who did it. It cost Farm one voice but did not save Blair.
Ellis's Floofer hugged Alex, Casey and Drew, which blanked three Farm roles in one night.

confusions.what: Said Drew's Falcon egg did not fit, misreading the Falcon rule (egg when the target visited no one).
Accused Drew on the same Falcon misreading, then retracted.
Also repeated the Falcon accusation against Drew.
Had the Turkey payout backwards at first, thinking a Turkey with no egg change meant nobody visited.
Said a Hawk gains only on a Meowfia target and thought Blair's Turkey visit was odd, then misread the Turkey payout.
Said Ellis should have gained two eggs as Turkey, forgetting visitors gain, not the Turkey.
Claimed Tit for a Turkey-visit egg, though the egg came from the Turkey, not a Tit guess.
Treated Drew's no-egg Hawk result as clearing Ellis, ignoring that Drew was hugged.
Called the Floofer visitor a Meowfia to watch, while having visited Ellis herself.
Used Blair's role claims from earlier rounds as evidence, though roles are re-dealt every round.

worked: Round 2's Turkey and Tit claims made a real puzzle: Blair's egg, the double Tit claim and Alex's Kookaburra result cross-checked into a correct Meowfia vote.
The Floofer hug in round 3 blanked three Farm roles and made a murky, interesting night.
Meowfia seeing a safe unused animal and the Wink gave real bluffing and removal options.
problems: Doubled banking for Meowfia plus +5 made round 1 worth about 90 points, while later rounds paid about 3 to 21. The score swing from round 1 decided the whole game, so rounds 2 and 3 had no tension. Fix: cap the double or scale it, or cap stake value.

Casey and Finley won round 1 by simply joining the likely mob vote. Meowfia has no need to hide when Farm piles on a random target. A Farm player's wrong accusation has no penalty, so bandwagons are cheap.

Round 1 had almost no usable information; roles like Tit, Hawk and Falcon gave little. Players argued over rule misreads instead of evidence, and the same Falcon, Turkey and Hawk misreadings repeated in several rounds. Add a rules reminder or clearer wording for who gains eggs.
Hug and Wink effects hide the source, so Farm cannot check anything. Ellis's triple hug in round 3 left nothing to deduce, and the winks removed Farm voices without changing outcomes.

Players cited roles from past rounds as evidence, though roles are re-dealt. Blair, as Meowfia, was a cheap and consistent scapegoat, and teammates threw nothing at their own partner. Ellis's refusal to stake cost nothing, so partner-sacrifice play is weakly punished.
